extracted.intended_audience: CIHR Project Grant peer reviewers, Committee Chairs, Scientific Officers and mock review participants (Canadian health researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation standards for conducting CIHR Project Grant peer review (used here for mock/simulation training). Covers reviewer recruitment, standards of practice, review quality checklist, adjudication criteria (Concept; Feasibility; Expertise/Resources), rating procedures and committee meeting processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Review Committee responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer Review Committees (PRCs) are responsible for: evaluating individual applications; rating each application; discussing applications at the face-to-face Committee meeting and voting on applications; recommending a budget and term to support the proposed research if the application is approved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: providing a budget recommendation is only included for the purposes of the Internal Simulation or if the Facilitator decides to include budget discussions as part of the simulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment criteria — Committee Chairs and Scientific Officers
rubrics_metrics.description: Chairs and Scientific Officers will be recruited based on a set of selection criteria including significant peer review experience, Independent Investigator status at a University or Research Institution, and holding Tri-Council funding (or equivalent) within the last 5 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significant experience includes participation in multiple review activities. To meet knowledge translation application requirements, Chairs/Scientific Officers may be recruited using a combination of the criteria as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment criteria — Peer reviewers: research experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers should have Independent Investigator status at a University or Research Institution and at least one recent federally funded (or equivalent) peer reviewed grant as a Principal Investigator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research experience criterion is used to ensure reviewers have direct programmatic research experience relevant to applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment criteria — Peer reviewers: review experience and training
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers should have at least two prior peer review roles and must complete training modules on bias in peer review and review quality, as well as learning modules on sex- and gender-based analysis in health research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completion of specified training modules is required to ensure reviewers are trained in review quality and bias-awareness prior to participating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment criteria — Knowledge, expertise and lived experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must have expertise within CIHR's mandate; knowledge users (when appropriate) will be recruited using selection combinations and integrated knowledge translation applications will be assessed by both researchers and knowledge user reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Knowledge users include practitioners, policy-makers, community leaders, etc.; recruitment may consider lived experience relevant to the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of Practice for Peer Review (SPPR)
rubrics_metrics.description: All Reviewers must sign and abide by the Standards of Practice for Peer Review Agreement which consolidates CIHR Peer Review Principles and Policies and outlines peer reviewer responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competition Chairs, Scientific Officers and Reviewers must consent prior to participating; those who do not consent cannot participate. Participants in the Toolkit exercise should read the SPPR in its entirety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Quality Assurance (RQA) — Appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriateness: Review comments are fair, understandable, original, confidential and respectful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation includes respecting the Conflict of Interest and Confidentiality Policy; absence of comments suggesting bias (sex, ethnicity, age, language, career stage, affiliation, geography); clear and understandable language; avoid sarcastic, flippant or arrogant comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Quality Assurance (RQA) — Robustness
rubrics_metrics.description: Robustness: Review is thorough, complete and credible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review must contain a detailed justification of the rating, meaningful descriptions of strengths and weaknesses, alignment of comments with the rating, address all applicable adjudication criteria, ensure all relevant sections are complete (Budget Recommendation, Sex/Gender considerations), factual correctness, and avoid statements that call into question the reviewer's expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Quality Assurance (RQA) — Utility
rubrics_metrics.description: Utility: Review provides feedback that addresses the needs of reviewers, applicants and funders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should be constructive and help applicants improve future submissions; provide information allowing other reviewers to understand the rating; be detailed enough for CIHR to evaluate and refine review process elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements of a Review — Project summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers provide a summary of the project to demonstrate their understanding of the research work being proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The summary demonstrates comprehension and frames the reviewer's subsequent assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements of a Review — Summary of Progress
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must assess the Summary of Progress (when provided): it contextualizes results supporting the current application; explains how the application fits within the applicant's research program and why funds are needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should outline how current budget request is distinct from funds already held or overlaps with pending grants; outline impact of factors (leave, COVID-19) on progress. The Summary of Progress is narrative, not a detailed accounting—funding details are in the CV.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rating procedure and scale
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers provide an initial rating for each application to one decimal place in advance of the committee meeting; reviewers are not bound by this initial rating and may change it during the meeting. The rating scale ranges from 0.0–4.9.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Descriptors and ranges: Outstanding 4.5–4.9; Excellent 4.0–4.4; Good 3.5–3.9; Fair 3.0–3.4; Poor 0.0–2.9. Reviewers are encouraged to use the full range of the scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengths and weaknesses requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must highlight the strengths and weaknesses of the proposal based on the evaluation criteria and are encouraged to provide strengths/weaknesses for each evaluation criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengths and weaknesses that contributed to the application rating must be clearly articulated because they are used to justify the rating to other reviewers and to provide feedback to applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of Sex and/or Gender (SGBA) assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers comment on whether sex (biological) and/or gender (socio-cultural) integration in the proposal is a strength, a weakness, or not applicable, and provide recommendations to improve integration where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessors should complete training modules on sex/gender considerations, read the 'Other Project Information' section for applicant statements, critically assess the full proposal for appropriate integration or justified exclusion, and incorporate assessment into the overall score (under Approaches and Methods) if applicable. Discuss SGBA in committee prior to consensus scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: DORA considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must assess productivity broadly (not just publications) and consider applicant context (career stage, leave history) in line with the San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment (DORA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scholarly outputs may include non-journal outputs; DORA principles apply across adjudication criteria but are especially important for Expertise, Experience and Resources. Reviewers are directed to DORA materials and examples of misaligned comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artificial Intelligence (AI) considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are responsible for reading applications and writing fair and rigorous reviews. Copying and pasting application materials into AI platforms may constitute a breach of confidentiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plagiarism matters are covered by the Tri-Agency Framework: Responsible Conduct of Research. Reviewers should be familiar with College guidelines on Review Quality; guidance on AI is evolving and CIHR is working with Tri-agency colleagues on consistent community guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjudication Criterion 1 — Concept: Significance and Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the project idea is creative and among the best in its field; whether the rationale is sound; whether goals and objectives are well-defined; and whether anticipated contributions are likely to advance basic health-related knowledge, health care, systems, or outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider new, incremental, innovative, or high-risk lines of inquiry; include knowledge translation/commercialization where appropriate; anticipated contributions should be substantive, realistic and aligned to objectives. This sub-criterion does not assess feasibility or team expertise (these are in Criterion 2). Indigenous Health Research and Global Health considerations apply as noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjudication Criterion 2 — Feasibility: Approaches and Methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether approaches and methods are appropriate and justified to deliver proposed outputs and achieve contributions; whether sex/gender is appropriately considered; timelines realistic; and potential challenges and mitigation strategies are identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opportunities to maximize contributions should be sought and planned for. For Indigenous Health Research, approaches must respect Indigenous values/ways of knowing and follow relevant TCPS2 Chapter 9 or agreed governance. Knowledge translation approaches should be appropriate when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjudication Criterion 3 — Expertise, Experience and Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the applicant team brings appropriate combined expertise and experience to lead and deliver outputs and achieve contributions; whether roles and responsibilities are clearly described and linked to objectives; level of engagement/commitment is appropriate; and whether the environment supports project success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider access to infrastructure, facilities, personnel, equipment and supplies; demonstrate productivity and progress in the Summary of Progress (if present); assess team appropriateness for Indigenous research including lived experience; consider leaves-of-absence supplements to publication records; account for networked or partnered environments for resource support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget recommendation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget assessment must not be factored into the scientific assessment and must not influence the rating of applications; reviewers may recommend budgets and terms but CIHR reserves the final award amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the simulation, budget and term will not be evaluated unless participating in an Internal Simulation with real applications. See Project Peer Review Manual for additional detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of Interest and confidentiality — assignment and signing
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are assigned to reviewers who identify conflicts of interest and declare their ability to review; Reviewers must sign the Conflict of Interest and Confidentiality Agreement (in simulation) prior to receiving applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignment of three reviewers is based on declared level of expertise. In simulations reviewers also may be asked to declare Ability to Review. Chairs and Scientific Officers, with CIHR staff, manage assignments according to policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application assignment to PRCs and reassignment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are initially assigned to the applicant's first-choice committee; CIHR staff review assignments and may split committees or reassign applications based on committee mandate; final authority for assignment rests with CIHR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chairs and Scientific Officers review assignments; committees may be split if application pressure is high; for simulation a single Scientific Officer per committee may be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee meeting sequence, roles and consensus procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequence of steps for committee meetings: overview; application initial ratings; reviewers present application and reviews (primary ~5 min, secondaries follow); committee discussion moderated by Chair; Scientific Officer takes notes; consensus rating by assigned reviewers; committee individual ratings collected; matters flagged; Scientific Officer reads final notes; optional debrief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consensus: assigned reviewers attempt to reach consensus rating using Rating Scale; if consensus cannot be reached the Chair determines consensus rating by averaging the assigned Reviewers' ratings after discussion. Committee individual ratings may vote +/-0.5 from assigned reviewers' consensus score. Chairs and Scientific Officers do not vote. The Chair manages conflicts of interest (announces conflicted reviewers who leave the room).

rubrics_metrics.name: Matters to be flagged during committee
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee should flag ethics issues, eligibility, use of human stem cells, other concerns, and research of general interest (especially highly rated/ranked applications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flagged matters should be recorded in Scientific Officer notes and validated/approved by the committee; SGBA comments should be recorded prior to consensus scoring if not addressed by assigned reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of French language applications
rubrics_metrics.description: CIHR allows applications submitted in French two additional pages of research proposal in the Project Grant Competition (as of 2019) to ensure equitable space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision is intended to equalize space as documents written in French require approximately 20% more space than similar documents in English; reviewers should account for this when assessing application length/clarity.
